entries.definition: Behavior that is correct and polite for a formal occasion.
entries.example: She greeted the ambassador with perfect decorum.

entries.definition: Cool and distant, not wanting to join in friendly talk.
entries.example: His aloof greeting made the newcomers hesitate.

entries.definition: Easy to talk to, pleasant, and good-natured.
entries.example: The affable chair put every guest at ease within a minute.

entries.definition: Done quickly and without real feeling, because it is expected.
entries.example: He gave a perfunctory hello and returned to his phone.

entries.definition: Polite respect you show to someone of higher status or age.
entries.example: Younger staff showed deference by greeting the director first.

entries.definition: A relaxed closeness that can be friendly or, sometimes, too casual.
entries.example: Using a nickname too soon can suggest unwanted familiarity.

entries.definition: A first move toward friendship, talk, or agreement.
entries.example: She appreciated his friendly overture at the reception.

entries.definition: To become friendly again after a disagreement or a cold distance.
entries.example: I hope the two friends reconcile at the reunion.

entries.definition: Stiff and unnatural, especially in speech or manners.
entries.example: The conversation stayed stilted until someone laughed.

entries.definition: Cheerful and friendly, in a way that makes people enjoy being together.
entries.example: A convivial host can rescue even a formal reception.

entries.headword: allow me to extend a welcome
entries.definition: A formal way to greet a guest on behalf of a group.
entries.example: Allow me to extend a welcome to our visitors from Osaka.

entries.headword: I trust you had a pleasant journey
entries.definition: A formal, polite question-like remark after someone arrives from a trip.
entries.example: I trust you had a pleasant journey. May I take your coat?

entries.headword: we appear to have started off badly
entries.definition: A careful way to say a relationship began with a misunderstanding.
entries.example: We appear to have started off badly, and I would like to put that right.

entries.definition: A very formal way to introduce one person to another.
entries.example: May I present Dr Okonkwo, who is joining us this evening.

entries.definition: To follow the official rules for a formal greeting or event.
entries.example: Junior staff observe protocol and greet the chair first.

entries.definition: An action that breaks a polite social rule.
entries.example: Using a nickname too soon can be a breach of etiquette.

entries.definition: A first friendly action meant to open a relationship.
entries.example: Ignoring a social overture can feel like a snub.

entries.definition: A person both speakers know, though neither is close to them.
entries.example: We found we had a mutual acquaintance at the embassy.

entries.headword: get off on the wrong foot
entries.definition: To begin a relationship or activity in an unfortunate way.
entries.example: I do not want us to get off on the wrong foot, so let me explain.

entries.definition: To annoy a person without necessarily intending to.
entries.example: A cold greeting can rub someone the wrong way at a party.

entries.definition: Knowing someone only well enough to nod when you meet.
entries.example: We are on nodding terms, but I have never learned his name.
